newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end sharply up as electronics rise.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end sharply up as electronics rise.

text.p: Strong buying in blue chip electronics pushed Taiwan share prices to finish sharply higher on Thursday, but brokers said it was too early to say whether the index has finished a recent consolidation.

The weighted index ended 121.68 points or 1.52 percent higher at 8,144.57, off a 8,157.80 high. Turnover improved to T$90 billion, still slack compared to its first-quarter bull run but well above Wednesday's T$67 billion.
Chipmakers and other electronics rose 3.8 percent. Brokers attributed the rebound to hopes for sound third-quarter profits and an export boost from an easy Taiwan dollar depreciation.
Many investors had dumped integrated circuit shares after their stellar first-quarter rise and the recent announcement of less than spectacular first-quarter results.

"Some electronics might have been over-vauled in the first quarter, but the outlooks are still promising as the sector is entering its traditional hot sales season, said Oliver Fang, an analyst of National Securities.
Grand Cathay Securities' analyst Mike Tsai is optimistic.
"Compared with other sectors, Taiwan electronic companies are still very competitive," Tsai said.

Analysts have said strength in the star electronics industry had helped to ensure stable growth in Taiwan's April export orders and industrial output, helping to overcome major export damage arising from a hog farm epidemic and port export ban.
Chipmaker United Microelectronics Corp rose T$3 or 4.44 percent to T$70.5 after active trade.
Plastics were also strong, up 3.70 percent. Blue chip Nan Ya Plastics gained T$2.5 or 3.62 percent to T$71.5.
China Steel was the most actively traded issue after its announcement of third-quarter price increases. Its share price rose 40 cents or 1.33 percent to T$30.5.
